title: Short Stuff: Sitzpinklers Unite
summary: Short Stuff episode in which Josh and Chuck (with Ben sitting in) discuss sitting down to urinate ("sitzpinkling"), starting with a brief birthday exchange. They cover a survey of Western countries and Japan showing rising rates of men sitting to pee, German cultural campaigns (starting around 2004) to get men to sit, German toilet gadgets with voice prompts, the hygiene argument (urine splash and droplet breakup when standing), the claim of research from a Utah university on urine backspray, porcelain's splatter properties, emptying the bladder and prostate concerns, and personal anecdotes about switching to sitting, especially at night.

segments.title: Opening banter and birthday
segments.summary: Josh introduces the episode with Ben sitting in for Jerry. Chuck and Josh chat about Josh's birthday and social media posts.

segments.title: Sitting down to pee
segments.summary: Chuck and Josh admit they sit down to urinate, with Josh calling himself a sitzpinkler and noting he still stands in public restrooms. Chuck recounts his brother-in-law, who is German, as the first adult man he saw doing it.

segments.title: International survey of men who sit to pee
segments.summary: The hosts discuss a survey of Western countries plus the US, Canada, Mexico, Australia and Singapore on how often men sit to urinate. Germany led at 62 percent (every or most times), followed by Sweden at 50, Denmark at 44, and Australia at 39. The US, Mexico, Britain and Singapore came in between 20 and 24 percent.

segments.title: German campaign to get men sitting
segments.summary: Josh explains that sitting to pee was once an insult in Germany, and that a campaign starting around 2004 aimed to train German men to sit. Chuck describes a German toilet device with a recorded voice message, which Josh says is triggered when the lid is lifted.

segments.title: Japan's rise in sitting to pee
segments.summary: Josh says Japan saw a similar shift around 2000. A survey found 15 percent of Japanese men sat to urinate in 1999, rising to 60 percent by 2020. The hosts say they will come back to the reasons for the change.

segments.title: Why the trend grew: hygiene
segments.summary: Chuck says he could not find a pop culture cause, such as a movie, and suggests the change is men recognizing that sitting is more hygienic and reduces urine outside the bowl.

segments.title: Urine splatter and distracted urination
segments.summary: Josh says standing to urinate almost always results in some urine landing outside the toilet, while sitting makes that nearly zero. Chuck and Josh joke about men on phones at urinals and missing the target.

segments.title: Fluid dynamics of urine backspray
segments.summary: Chuck cites a Utah university physics department study on urine backspray, saying some spray is likely even when standing correctly. Josh explains the stream breaks into droplets after about six inches due to the plateau-Rayleigh instability. Chuck adds that porcelain is hydrophilic and splatters.

segments.title: Bladder emptying and prostate
segments.summary: Josh says people who favor sitting emphasize emptying the bladder fully. Medical researchers say either position may make no difference depending on health and prostate condition. Chuck shares his own prostate-related change in urination.
topics: medical debate on sitting to pee

segments.title: Women and standing urination
segments.summary: Chuck notes women lack the prostate's support and can have difficulty emptying the bladder when forced to urinate standing up. Josh says sitting helps bladder emptying, though hovering over a public seat has similar problems.

segments.title: Nighttime and personal anecdotes
segments.summary: Chuck says nighttime trips to the bathroom were what got him to sit down. Josh recalls accidentally sitting down mid-stream the first time he did it.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh closes the episode and gives the iHeartRadio production credit and podcast app information.
